study.title: Deep-Learning-Based Registration of Diagnostic Angiogram and Live Fluoroscopy for Percutaneous Coronary Intervention

imaging.modality_detail: Diagnostic coronary angiography cine loops and live fluoroscopy during PCI (512x512, 8-bit grayscale)
imaging.territory_detail: Coronary arteries during percutaneous coronary intervention (guidewire navigation)
imaging.frames_per_sequence: Angiographic sequence mean ~15.8 frames; live fluoroscopy mean 146.5 frames per patient

task.task_description: Patient-specific U-Net generative model registers diagnostic angiographic frames to segmented guidewire images from live fluoroscopy (dynamic coronary roadmapping) without ECG, implicitly compensating cardiac and respiratory motion; trained on virtual guidewires synthesized from angiographic centerlines, with ICP post-processing and transfer learning to shorten training.
task.clinical_application: Dynamic coronary roadmapping for guidewire navigation during PCI, including arrhythmia patients

temporal_evidence.quote: used as training input to a deep generative model along with stacked images of the angiographic sequence

method.pretraining: Transfer learning (fine-tuning) from a patient-specific model pre-trained on another patient's data with the same C-arm configuration

metrics.metric: Overlay quality rated Good by cardiologists
Overlay quality rated Acceptable by cardiologists
Mean processing time per live fluoroscopic frame

comparators: Ma et al. catheter tip tracking DCR with deep-learning-based Bayesian filtering
Learning from scratch vs transfer learning
U-Net variants with different depth and filters

G1.quote: The proposed deep generative model is trained patientspecifically because only a small amount of PCI data is available.

G2.quote: the average mean tPSNR (34.09 dB) was lower than the average mean vPSNR (38.36 dB) because the segmented real guidewire images were slightly different from the virtual guidewire images

G3.quote: This is because the generative model does not use temporal information during image generation. This problem may be solved by incorporating temporal information into the generative model.

G5.quote: To address the lack of labeled data (ground-truth registered images) for training the deep generative model, we used the centerline of the coronary artery in the angiographic sequence as an approximated real guidewire

G6.quote: for practical usage, further reducing training time and automatic centerline labeling of blood vessels and clinical evaluation remain.

G9.quote: Only three arrhythmia cases were used in this study, requiring more evaluation for robustness.

other_limitations: Long patient-specific training time (about 2 h) not feasible online without transfer learning
Manual centerline labeling of angiographic sequence required
Assumes identical C-arm configuration between diagnostic and interventional phases
ICP/centerline-based registration error may not properly indicate registration quality
No ground-truth registered images available for direct evaluation
future_work: Automatic centerline labeling of angiographic sequences
Automatic real-time guidewire segmentation from live fluoroscopy
GAN-based image-to-image translation to make virtual guidewire images more realistic
Select pre-trained model with most similar vessel structure to shorten training
Optimize data augmentation and hardware acceleration (multi-GPU, FPGA, ASIC)
Incorporate temporal information into the generative model and further clinical evaluation
